content: <thought>Based on the ESI‑MS spectrum the most intense ion is at m/z 183.0451, which corresponds to the [M+H]⁺ ion. Subtracting the mass of a proton gives a neutral monoisotopic mass of ≈ 182.0378 Da. The strong M+2 peak (~33 % of the base peak) is characteristic of a single chlorine atom (⁷⁵Cl/³⁷Cl isotopic pattern). Accounting for one Cl (34.9689 Da) leaves ≈ 147.069 Da to be composed of C, H, N and O. The formula C₆H₁₃ClNO₃ matches this residual mass (182.0584 Da) within a few mDa and reproduces the observed isotopic pattern (M+1 ≈ 10 % from ¹³C and ¹⁵N, M+2 ≈ 33 % from ³⁷Cl). Therefore the most plausible molecular formula is **C6H13ClNO3**.
